objectives.title: Send a request against your API
objectives.why: Seeing a real response is the fastest way to find out your API doesn't behave the way the spec claims.

objectives.title: Generate an OpenAPI spec from your codebase
objectives.why: A spec makes your API documented, mockable, and testable — the foundation for everything else.

objectives.title: Search for an existing API before building your own
objectives.why: The integration you're about to hand-roll may already exist as a maintained collection.

objectives.title: Sync your spec to a Postman collection
objectives.why: A collection generated from the spec keeps your requests and your contract from drifting apart.

objectives.title: Create a mock server for frontend development
objectives.why: Mocks let the frontend build against realistic responses before the API is done.

objectives.title: Save example responses on your requests
objectives.why: Examples are what your mock server returns and what your published docs show — without them both are empty shells.

objectives.title: Move base URLs and secrets into an environment
objectives.why: Hardcoded hosts and tokens in requests leak into git and make the same collection unusable against staging.

objectives.title: Run your collection as tests
objectives.why: Running the collection turns your requests into a repeatable test suite.

objectives.title: Security-audit your API (OWASP API Top 10)
objectives.why: Catch the common API vulnerabilities before they ship.

objectives.title: Publish your API documentation
objectives.why: Published docs are how anyone else — human or agent — discovers what your API can do.

objectives.title: Automate a multi-step workflow with Flows
objectives.why: Chaining calls in a Flow beats a scratch script nobody else can run or debug.

objectives.title: Bootstrap your repo's Postman workspace
objectives.why: Binding the repo to a workspace and initializing local API files is what lets every later step produce files you can review in Git rather than state that lives only in the cloud.

objectives.title: Run your code against simulated dependencies
objectives.why: Running a service against stand-ins for the APIs it calls shows how it behaves when a dependency is slow, wrong or down — without needing the real ones.

objectives.title: Check real application traffic against your API contract
objectives.why: Playwright tests already exercise your app — matching the network traffic they capture against the collection finds the calls that drift from the contract.

objectives.title: Monitor a live endpoint
objectives.why: A monitor reuses your collection's assertions on a schedule, so a regression is caught by a check rather than by a user.

objectives.title: Capture and replay webhooks
objectives.why: A reusable public URL records deliveries even when your local server is down, which separates 'the sender never sent it' from 'my machine wasn't listening'.

objectives.title: Load-test your API
objectives.why: Latency and error thresholds under concurrent users are a different question from 'does it return 200', and you'd rather learn the answer before launch.

objectives.title: Score how ready your API is for AI agents
objectives.why: A measured score turns 'agents struggle with our API' into a list of specific contract gaps to fix.

objectives.title: Drive a collection from a dataset
objectives.why: Queried or joined inputs let one collection cover many cases instead of copying requests per case.

bestPractices.title: Keep your Postman API key out of git
bestPractices.why: Secrets in git are secrets leaked.

bestPractices.title: Describe your endpoints well enough for AI agents
bestPractices.why: Clear summaries and named params are what let AI agents actually use your API.

criteria.rubric: Do the operations have clear summaries/descriptions and named, described parameters suitable for an AI agent to call?

bestPractices.title: Gate CI on contract checks
bestPractices.why: Tests, lint and AI-readiness checks that only run when someone remembers to run them don't protect the main branch; a CI gate does.
